# the contributor audit: shared-plane transfer, radial trap, and coordinated escape

## One shared original plane

The root fully read `candidate 49cf658d249b7638`
and ran its exact verifier: PASS. The constraint v_e=0 keeps the actual
shared cap plane fixed along the entire path, not merely its first
derivative. The remaining sum-zero space has dimension d-1 and inherits
the previously proved isotropic positive Hessian. Body acceleration
cannot alter that plane equation. Every additional private cap's budget
must still be checked on the physically varied fiber; strict emptiness,
a strictly negative proper-trace derivative, and a strictly full trace
have exactly the three behaviors stated. In particular a full trace
blocks volume increase at all orders even though its first derivative
vanishes on a trace-zero critical mode.

The two explicit planar groups have the stated positive circuits and
projected margins. The displayed B matrix has zero column sums, trace
zero, and row sums 6v; the exact cap masses and strict traces agree with
the verifier. The second group is redundant, which is explicitly
acknowledged. The result does not solve shared incidence in an arbitrary
minimal cover, and its initial free-fiber hypothesis is not smuggled in
through a radial perturbation of additional cap budgets.

## Binary embedding of the finite radial obstruction

The root read `candidate 4e0a45efacd4af50`
and ran the independent verifier: PASS. Its base polytope has exactly
the stated 2^n+1 integer points. Extremality of each binary coordinate
forces a fiber representation to use only that same binary base. This
proves all actual integer sections, with the single nonvertex core
midpoint retaining its exact Minkowski average. The body is full
dimensional.

The affine isolators vanish at their assigned regular vertex and have
gap at least one elsewhere, including the core point with z=2. All
continuous supports remain strictly below the exclusion threshold two.
The isolated original caps are therefore counted once, retain their
listed masses, and cover their assigned actual fibers. Each has a strict
exclusive witness. The group count is 2^n-1, not 2^n; the isolated groups
cover S, not all ambient space. On core binary base zero, the core group
still covers the whole continuous fiber.

For n>=2 an unchanged exposed regular simplex centroid gives the exact
absolute lower bound B_cap, and the displayed cover gives its matching
global upper bound. The ratio and its positive gap above OC are exact.
For nearby radial changes, the isolators remain valid, each regular
scale is at most one, and total nondecrease forces core nondecrease.
The independently proved finite core obstruction then freezes its three
scales, and total mass freezes the rest. This is an all-fiber finite
radial obstruction, not merely a tangent-space computation. It is not
an obstruction to nonradial deformations.

## Coordinated unrotation

The root fully read `candidate 6f105c395022bb26`
and ran its verifier: PASS. The root had independently derived its
one-parameter areas and cap fractions before the complete proof was
written. The six middle vertices are the actual Minkowski hull, as the
displayed nonnegative cross-product polynomials show. Cyclic symmetry
equates all three cap masses. The normalized cap derivative has precisely
the stated polynomial numerator; its displayed regrouping is positive
throughout 0<t<1/3.

The common squared dilation lies strictly between the mass-normalizing
and cap-normalizing factors. Thus mass increases and every fixed cap
shrinks. The midpoint relation remains equality, so no unsupported
independent-fiber neighborhood is needed. The whole path and its
first derivatives are genuine, and the printed rational witness has
the verified strict signs. The original radial obstruction remains
valid because the endpoint shapes change relative to their fixed
cap normals.

In the binary embedding this path can be made arbitrarily small, keeping
all regular fibers and all cap planes fixed. Isolation persists; core
budgets decrease, regular budgets remain B_cap, and total mass increases.
The same unchanged regular center and the retained cover prove that
the new absolute maximum is still exactly B_cap. Hence normalized
maximum depth strictly decreases. This conclusion uses both the cover
upper bound and the actual center lower bound, not cap-budget changes
alone. A separate agent is writing the full transfer corollary.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
